sections.title: Negative answers
sections.content: On its own, nem works exactly like English "No." Placed right before a word, it flips that word's truth instead: nem vagyok ("I am not"), nem tea ("it isn't tea"). Same word, same rule, whether you're answering a question or contradicting a statement.

One nem, endless uses: swap it in front of practically anything you've learned so far — a name, an object, a verb — and you've made it negative. Very few languages let one word carry that much weight; enjoy the efficiency while it lasts, since later units add more nuance to negation.
